mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect reverses during a recovery quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust across at least three contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which raises real discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages in at least five out of the last ten instances.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of co-decline episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average and UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during at least five such episodes in the past three years.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a sustained supply expansion, which typically boosts corporate revenues and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least six out of the last ten such episodes.
